lessons.title: Comparing Two Biographies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare two biographical texts.
success_criteria: I can say one similarity between the two nurses.
I can say one difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about both nurses from the last two weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing the two biographies, discussing similarities and differences.
lessons.independent_task: Children record similarities and differences between Florence Nightingale and Mary Seacole.

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative comprehension skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family one way the two nurses were similar.

lessons.title: Comparing Data: Two Nurses Fact Table
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to organise and compare information in a simple table.
success_criteria: I can complete a comparison table.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the comparisons made in English.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model organising facts about the two nurses into a comparison table.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a comparison table and answer questions about it.
key_questions: Which nurse worked in the Crimea?
What do both nurses have in common?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add extra rows and answer detailed questions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note data organisation skill applied to a cross-curricular context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Make a comparison table about two things at home.

lessons.title: Timeline: Nightingale and Seacole
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to place two significant individuals on a shared timeline.
success_criteria: I can place both nurses on a timeline.
I can say who was born first.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the concept of a timeline.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model placing both nurses on a shared timeline using their birth dates and key events.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a timeline showing both nurses' lives and key events.

differentiation.greater_depth: Add multiple events for each nurse with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note chronological understanding comparing two individuals — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Create a timeline of two family members' lives together.

lessons.title: Using 'And' and 'But' to Compare
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use coordinating conjunctions to compare the two nurses.
success_criteria: I can use 'and' to join similar ideas.
I can use 'but' to join different ideas.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the comparisons made on Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using 'and' for similarities and 'but' for differences when comparing the nurses.
lessons.independent_task: Children write comparison sentences using 'and' and 'but'.

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ varied sentences using both conjunctions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note use of coordinating conjunctions — evidence for ENG.W3.
lessons.plenary: Share comparison sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Make up a sentence using 'and' or 'but' at home.

lessons.title: Missing Number Problems to 100
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve missing number problems within 100.
success_criteria: I can find a missing number in an addition sentence.
I can find a missing number in a subtraction sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap missing number problems within 20 from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving missing number problems within 100 (e.g. 45 + ? = 70).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve missing number problems within 100.
key_questions: How did you work it out?

differentiation.support: Solve missing number problems within 50 with a number line

lessons.assessment_notes: Record missing number problem-solving extending to 100 — evidence for MATHS.N2.

lessons.title: Which Nurse Do You Admire Most?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to state and justify an opinion about which nurse they admire most.
success_criteria: I can say which nurse I admire.
I can give a reason.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model stating an opinion with a reason: 'I admire ___ because ___.'
lessons.independent_task: Children write which nurse they admire most and why.
key_questions: Which nurse do you admire most?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note opinion formation with historical reasoning — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family which nurse they would admire and why.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Comparison Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read comparison-themed words fluently.
success_criteria: I can read comparison words.
I can read a comparison sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to comparison-themed words (e.g. 'same', 'different', 'both').
lessons.independent_task: Children read comparison sentence cards about the two nurses.
key_questions: Can you read this comparison sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading comparison words over the week.

lessons.title: Shape Properties: Comparing 2D Shapes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare properties of different 2D shapes.
success_criteria: I can compare two shapes' properties.
I can say a similarity and difference.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing properties of two different 2D shapes (e.g. square and rectangle).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare pairs of 2D shapes, recording similarities and differences in properties.
key_questions: What is similar about these shapes?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Compare two shapes you find at home.

lessons.title: Nurses Today: Are They Similar?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare Nightingale and Seacole's work to nurses today.
success_criteria: I can name something a nurse does today.
I can compare it to what these nurses did.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss similarities between the work of Nightingale/Seacole and nurses today (caring for the sick, hygiene).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare historical nursing to nursing today, recording similarities.
key_questions: What is similar about nursing then and now?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of historical understanding to the present day — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap nursing then and now comparisons.
lessons.home_link: Talk about nurses or doctors you know.

lessons.title: Class Debate: Nightingale or Seacole?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present and defend an opinion in a respectful debate.
success_criteria: I can present my opinion.
I can listen respectfully to a different view.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model respectful debate — presenting an opinion and listening to others.
lessons.independent_task: Children take part in a class debate about which nurse's achievements they find most inspiring, listening respectfully.
key_questions: What is your opinion and why?
How do you feel about a different opinion?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note discussion and evaluation of different viewpoints, a Year 2 spoken language objective — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the debate and range of views.
lessons.home_link: Debate which nurse is most inspiring with your family.

lessons.title: Times Tables Application: Comparing Totals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use times tables facts to compare totals in a real context.
success_criteria: I can calculate a total using times tables.
I can compare two totals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using times tables to calculate and compare totals (e.g. patients cared for over several days).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve times-table-based problems and compare totals.

differentiation.support: Use times table grids for support

lessons.assessment_notes: Record times table application to comparison problems — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Use times tables to compare two totals at home.

lessons.title: Creating a Comparison Poster
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a comparison of two significant individuals visually.
success_criteria: I can include facts about both nurses.
I can show a similarity and difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all facts gathered about both nurses.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model designing a comparison poster with sections for each nurse and shared facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a comparison poster about Florence Nightingale and Mary Seacole.
key_questions: What will you include for each nurse?
How will you show what they share?

differentiation.greater_depth: Include detailed facts and a personal opinion section

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis and presentation of comparative historical knowledge — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Show your poster to your family and explain the comparisons.

lessons.title: Comparing Nurses Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions comparing the two nurses.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage comparing the two nurses, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What did both nurses have in common?
Why might their approaches have differed?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family comparing the two nurses.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Data, Shape, Number
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply data, shape and number skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can compare data in a table.
I can compare shapes.
I can solve missing number problems.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's data, shape, and number learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: What is similar about these shapes?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 10 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.STAT/GEO/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising missing number problems over the weekend.

lessons.title: Significant Nurses Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise and compare key facts about Florence Nightingale and Mary Seacole.
success_criteria: I can name a fact about each nurse.
I can say a similarity and a difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole two-week topic on significant nurses.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the two weeks' learning comparing significant individuals.
lessons.independent_task: Children contribute to a final class display celebrating both nurses' achievements and comparisons.
key_questions: What have we learned about these two significant individuals?
lessons.assessment_notes: End of topic consolidation for the significant individuals unit — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished significant nurses display, celebrating two weeks of learning.
lessons.home_link: Share everything you learned about these two significant nurses with your family.
